sodiumSaltChange.rule: Same provider panel and compatible units/bases. Non-overlapping salt and 2.5 × sodium intervals must remain disjoint after retained uncertainty and supported possible sodium-label rounding. Missing or indeterminate precision is not itself a conflict.
sodiumSaltChange.rounding: 21 CFR 101.9(c)(4): inverse intervals for reported US per-serving declarations (zero below 5 mg; 5-mg increments through 140 mg; 10-mg increments above 140 mg; union at 140 mg). Propagate those bounds to equivalent reference/serving fields on the same mass/volume dimension. If original precision is unavailable, conservatively allow the largest FDA half-increment, 5 mg per compatible serving, as a possible explanation; salt may derive from such a rounded declaration. Retain any broader recorded uncertainty. No compatible serving means comparison indeterminate. These are uncertainty bounds, not replacement nutrients or verification of label compliance.
sodiumSaltChange.originalEvidence: Raw observations remain in assessmentInputs; gateway and remote provider snapshots retain published values. Effective candidates and new records use null disputed sodium plus separate nutritionConflicts. Salt may be provider-derived; neither observation is a verified replacement.
sodiumSaltChange.manufacturerScope: Complete manufacturer panels supersede provider conflicts without comparing manufacturer sodium to provider salt. Partial sugar corrections retain unresolved provider sodium; separately attributed manufacturer-reference comparisons stay separate.
sodiumSaltChange.cache: Existing cache conventions and provider order/timeouts unchanged. Retained sodium and salt evidence is re-evaluated at selection; missing old salt evidence alone never marks a cache conflict or forces refresh. No cache/storage clearing or historical migration.
